related_work: We looked back at ethnography. It is a way to study the life and culture of a group of people. Science research usually wants to prove something is true or false, but ethnography wants to find out what is really happening. We also learned some common methods, like surveys, interviews, focus groups and experiments. There are two kinds of data: quantitative data and qualitative data
conclusion_future_work: This class helped me understand that every project needs a clear research question first. Then I can choose the right methods and steps. Next, I want to think about what data I will collect, who my participants are, and how I can use a consent form to ask for their permission.
results_discussion: I learned a useful framework: method → techniques → procedures. Techniques include making prototypes, testing, observing people and getting feedback. Procedures can be a straight line, or a process where you try, change and try again (iteration). In group work, we shared the methods we will use in our own projects. We also talked about research ethics: before we collect data from people, we must get their consent first
title: week7
introduction: This class was about research methods. Our course is an MSc, but it is in an art school, so we need to use art methods and science methods together. The teacher said a research method answers the question “how”: how will I do my project?
